tool_input.command:
poetry run python - <<'PY'
import json
p="output_evaluation.json"
d=json.load(open(p))
for e in d["elements"]:
    s=sum(x["score"] for x in e["sub_elements"] if x["score"] is not None)
    na=sum(1 for x in e["sub_elements"] if x["score"] is None)
    print(e["id"], "recorded",e["element_score"],"computed",s,"max",e["element_max"],"na",na)
PY
tool_input.description: Recompute element sums from sub-element scores

This matches what I would expect of the current rules (the dedicated `updates.update_details` slot plus the anti-crediting clause), so I proceeded.

VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric10-semantic

**Score: 34/50 — fixed 68.0% (34/50), normalized 68.0% (34/50).** No sub-element was excluded: all five trigger conditions resolve as met (human subjects via E1 description/keywords and E8 collection mechanisms; governance via E2 `confidentiality_level: restricted`; datasets-shared via `distribution_formats` + `third_party_sharing.is_shared` + two documented access routes; software-output via the `chorus-ai` GitHub org in `external_resources`; collection via `acquisition_methods`/`collection_mechanisms`). Element scores: E1 3, E2 4, E3 4, E4 2, E5 3, E6 2, E7 5, E8 5, E9 4, E10 2.

Deidentification (per-modality, tool-named) and privacy protections (four named artefacts) do pass.
